(chosen; the team's prior decision)", "[Session model] Sticky sessions: balancer affinity cookie...", "[Session model] Signed cookies: the whole session in the browser, signed by the server" and "**Baseline: do nothing**".

expectations.text: Writes a new record file at docs/adrs/0003-<slug>.md, numbered one above the highest existing record
expectations.evidence: Wrote docs/adrs/0003-keep-sessions-in-a-shared-store.md; existing records are 0001 and 0002, so 0003 is one above the highest.

expectations.text: The record's title states the decision taken (e.g. keep sessions in a shared store), not the problem or a product name
expectations.evidence: Title "# 3. Keep sessions in a shared store" states the decision taken.

expectations.text: The record uses exactly Nygard's sections as the existing records do (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences) and adds no other section such as Requirements, Options or Confirmation
expectations.evidence: Headings are exactly "## Status", "## Context", "## Decision", "## Consequences"; no other headings or labelled sub-blocks. Rejected options are prose inside Decision (reply: "states each rejected option at its best inside the Decision section, since Nygard has no Options section").

expectations.text: The record's Context states the problem and the decision drivers in priority order
expectations.evidence: Context opens with the problem ("each replica keeps the logins it created in its own memory, so a user is logged out when the balancer sends a new connection to another replica, and every deploy ... logs out every user") then "Drivers, in order: logout ends the session at once on every replica; users stay logged in across replicas and deploys; the fix must not bring back the single-instance outages ADR 2 removed; a session holds up to 20 KB...".

expectations.text: Each rejected option appears in the record with what it offers and the driver it fails
expectations.evidence: Sticky ("need no new service and add no latency, but each deploy's restart still logs out that replica's users"), signed cookies, revocation list and replication each give an offer and a failed driver. But "Doing nothing keeps users being logged out on deploys and replica changes" states no offer, and three options rejected in the document's tradeoff table are absent from the record: "[Buy] Hosted identity provider", "[Replica count] Go back to one web instance", "[Store engine] Table in a relational database". Not every rejected option appears.

claims.claim: Browsers are only required to keep 4,096 bytes per cookie (RFC 6265, section 6.1)
claims.evidence: RFC 6265 6.1 sets minimum capabilities of at least 4096 bytes per cookie; record and document cite it correctly.

claims.claim: Signed 20 KB session split over 7 or more cookies adds about 27 KB to every request (20 KB x 4/3 for base64)
ADR 0002 is untouched and not superseded
claims.evidence: Caller verified 0002 unmodified; record does not mark it.

claims.claim: The record links the full document
claims.evidence: It does not; it defers the link to a future PR URL, which the reply flags as a to-do.

uncertainties: 20 KB session size, traffic, deploy frequency and balancer routing are assumed (no application code in repo)
needs_review: Replace 'carried in the pull request' wording in record 0003 with a real link
workarounds: Kept the full document outside the repo because the repo has no design-doc location; skipped review checkpoints, assumptions stated inline

suggestions.assertion: The record uses exactly Nygard's sections as the existing records do (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences) and adds no other section such as Requirements, Options or Confirmation
suggestions.reason: Discriminates only if labelled inline blocks ("Options considered:", "Confirmation:") count as sections; reword to say 'no extra headings or labelled blocks' to make grading unambiguous.

suggestions.assertion: The record's Context states the problem and the decision drivers in priority order
suggestions.reason: Discriminates: with_skill writes 'Drivers, in order:' in Context; old_skill has no driver list.

suggestions.assertion: Each rejected option appears in the record with what it offers and the driver it fails
suggestions.reason: Fails both; ambiguous whether 'each rejected option' means every row of the document's table or only the options the user raised. Specify the set (e.g. sticky, signed cookies, baseline).

suggestions.assertion: The record links the full document
suggestions.reason: Fails both, for different reasons (with_skill defers to a PR URL because the document lives outside the repo; old_skill omits any reference). Clarify whether naming the document plus a placeholder counts, or whether the eval setup should give the document a repo path.

A1-A3, A8, A9 pass for both and do not discriminate. Missing: an assertion that the record stays short like 0001/0002, and one that the record does not repeat implementation detail (store config, rollout) that belongs in the document.

eval_feedback.overall: Discriminating assertions are A4 (sections) and A5 (ranked drivers in Context), both favouring with_skill. A6 and A7 fail both runs and need sharper wording; the rest are non-discriminating sanity checks.
